剛 concerns strength, sturdiness or an unyielding quality, physically or in character. 剛健 ごうけん describes robust bodily or mental vigor; 剛性 ごうせい means stiffness or rigidity.

These are recognition examples, not a claim that every compound is everyday vocabulary.

The indexing radical is 刀; its visible form here is 刂. 削, "shave; sharpen; pare," 剖, "dissect; split open," and 則, "rule; follow a model," share right-hand 刂 but have different left blocks and meanings.

強 also concerns strength, and 力 power. Their meanings overlap with 剛; they are not mutually exclusive categories. For the everyday adjective "strong," learn 強い つよい rather than treating 剛 as a general standalone replacement.
JMdict indexes 剛い under つよい as a search-only spelling. That is not a recommendation to write the ordinary adjective that way.

剛健 ごうけん — robust; vigorous
剛健 describes being robust and strong in body or spirit. It is a noun and a na-adjective: 剛健な + noun, or 剛健です as a polite predicate.
Digital Daijisen gives the phrase 勤勉で剛健な気風 (きんべんでごうけんなきふう), "a hardworking and robust spirit." Here 気風 means a characteristic spirit or ethos, and な connects 剛健 to that noun.
The expression 質実剛健 (しつじつごうけん) combines being plain and sincere with fortitude and vigor. It does not simply mean being cheerful or busy.

剛 contributes strength or sturdiness, and 健 contributes health or strength. The related meanings reinforce the idea of robust vigor. The on readings here are ゴウ + ケン. This is a meaning aid, not a reconstruction of the word's history.

丈夫 じょうぶ can describe a robust constitution and also durable objects. 健康 けんこう concerns health; 元気 げんき can emphasize being well or energetic. These meanings overlap, but 剛健 emphasizes robust strength rather than just a momentary lively mood.

強い つよい is a broader adjective for strength or intensity. 弱い よわい, "weak," gives a contextual contrast, not a judgment of a person's worth. There is no single opposite covering every bodily and mental use.

Japanese dictionaries describe a traditional masculine association in 剛健. That association is part of its connotation, not a grammatical restriction to male subjects or a rule about who can be strong.
Learn 剛健 as an adjective/noun, not as an i-adjective or an automatic する verb. It describes a robust quality; it is not the general word for every vigorous activity or every English use of "strong."
